intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Walk across the historic Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque, admiring its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide to uncover the layered Byzantine and Ottoman history embedded in every stone.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Market Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the vibrant Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, saffron, and local teas. Engage with vendors, practice bargaining, and taste free samples of authentic spices and sweets. A feast for all the senses and a deep dive into Ottoman mercantile culture.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Strait Ferry & Waterfront Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Board a public ferry for a scenic cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, the waterway dividing Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, ancient fortresses, and charming fishing villages. Disembark at Kadıköy on the Asian side and explore its lively market streets before sitting down to a fresh seafood lunch at a local meyhane (tavern), sampling grilled fish, meze platters, and raki.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Ottoman Imperial History Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Harem, the Treasury housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and the sacred relics pavilion. The palace complex offers breathtaking panoramic views over the Golden Horn and Bosphorus, making it one of the most historically rich sites in the world.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class & Bazaar Ingredient Hunt
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef who first takes you to a neighborhood market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare classic Turkish dishes such as börek, mercimek çorbası (lentil soup), stuffed grape leaves, and baklava. Enjoy your creations over a communal meal paired with Turkish tea, gaining authentic insight into the culinary traditions and family culture of Istanbul.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro to the city center (budget-friendly option, ~50-80 TRY vs expensive taxis). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack near the hotel and rest.

meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night simit (sesame bread ring) and ayran from a 24-hour street vendor or bakkal (corner shop) near the hotel — under 50 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Keep cash in Turkish Lira handy for transport. Download the Istanbul Kart app or buy an Istanbulkart at the airport for cheap public transit. Save receipts for budget tracking.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning. Walk to a local kahvaltı (Turkish breakfast) spot near the hotel. Then stroll along the nearby waterfront or neighborhood streets to orient yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Sultanahmet historic district. Visit the Hagia Sophia (free entry for exterior, modest fee inside). Walk to the nearby Sultanahmet Square and admire the Blue Mosque exterior. Explore the Hippodrome and the ancient Column of Constantine — all free.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Sultanahmet's atmospheric streets at dusk. Watch the Blue Mosque light up at night. Return to the hotel via tram or bus.

meals.breakfast: Local kahvaltı spread at a neighborhood café — tea, olives, cheese, eggs, bread for ~80-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Lahmacun (Turkish flatbread pizza) from a local eatery in Sultanahmet — ~40-60 TRY
meals.dinner: Köfteci (meatball restaurant) near the hotel — a full plate of köfte with bread and salad for ~100-140 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Dress modestly for mosque visits (cover shoulders and knees). The Istanbulkart makes tram rides very affordable (~15-20 TRY per trip).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Topkapi Palace (entrance ~350-400 TRY, skip the Harem add-on to save money). Explore the Imperial Treasury, the kitchens, and the stunning views of the Bosphorus from the palace terraces. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Gülhane Park — free and beautiful in May with spring blooms. Then explore the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex (one ticket covers three museums, ~200 TRY — excellent value for history lovers).
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram to the Eminönü waterfront. Buy a freshly grilled balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the iconic boats moored at the dock. Sit by the Galata Bridge and watch fishermen cast their lines as the sun sets over the Golden Horn.

meals.breakfast: Simit with tea from a street cart near the hotel — ~20-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a börek (savory pastry) from a bakery near Topkapi — ~50-70 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek at Eminönü waterfront + ayran — ~80-100 TRY total

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapi tickets online in advance to save time queuing. Topkapi is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — free entry, open from 8:30 AM. Don't feel pressured to buy; enjoy the labyrinthine corridors, colorful textiles, spices, ceramics, and lamps. Practice your bargaining skills if you do shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) — also free entry. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, and spices. Then walk along the Golden Horn waterfront toward the Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a hidden gem with exquisite Iznik tile work (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Eminönü and Sirkeci neighborhoods. Visit the historic Sirkeci Train Station (free, famous as the terminus of the Orient Express). Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local lokanta (traditional cafeteria-style restaurant).

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı salon near the hotel — ~100 TRY
meals.lunch: Mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and bread at a lokanta near the Spice Bazaar — ~60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Pide (Turkish flatbread with toppings) at a neighborhood pide salonu — ~120-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Keep a close eye on your belongings in crowded bazaars. Many vendors will offer free tea — it's a cultural tradition, not an obligation to buy.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot (free) and climb up to the Galata Tower area. The tower itself charges an entrance fee (~250 TRY), but the surrounding Galata neighborhood is free to explore — charming cobblestone streets, independent bookshops, and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up İstiklal Avenue — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard. Browse the historic arcade passages (pasajlar), street musicians, and independent shops. Detour to explore the Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market) in Beyoğlu.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Taksim Square area or find a rooftop café with a view. Then explore the lively Beyoğlu backstreets for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local café in Galata — ~80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Döner kebab wrap from a street stall on İstiklal Avenue — ~60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Meze plates and piyaz (bean salad) at a meyhane (tavern) in Beyoğlu — ~150-180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is very walkable and lively. The nostalgic red tram on İstiklal is a fun (cheap) ride. Beyoğlu has a vibrant nightlife scene if you want to explore after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to the Bosphorus — a classic Istanbul experience. Opt for the public IDO/BUDO ferry (Istanbulkart accepted, ~25-40 TRY) rather than tourist cruises. Enjoy views of palaces, mosques, and the two continents as you cruise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Üsküdar on the Asian side. Explore this charming, more traditional neighborhood. Visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque (free), stroll along the Asian waterfront, and enjoy panoramic views back toward the European skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to the European side as the sun sets — magical golden light on the minarets. Dinner in the Karaköy neighborhood, known for its hip local eateries.

meals.breakfast: Simit and tea at the ferry terminal — ~25-35 TRY
meals.lunch: Kokoreç (offal sandwich) or fresh fish at a casual Üsküdar waterfront eatery — ~80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Hummus, falafel, and mezze at a Karaköy restaurant — ~130-160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. Check IDO ferry schedules in advance. Üsküdar is generally quieter and more authentically local than Sultanahmet.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque and less crowded than the Blue Mosque (free entry). Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) with its historic medrese (seminary) buildings and beautiful gardens with Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most historically rich and authentically local districts. Visit the Fatih Mosque, explore the local street market (if running), and browse the traditional shops selling fabrics, herbs, and household goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for the free Sound and Light show at the Blue Mosque (seasonal, check schedule). Walk the ancient Byzantine walls section near Sultanahmet at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street vendor near the hotel — ~60-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at a Fatih neighborhood lokanta — ~70-90 TRY
meals.dinner: Kebab plate at a no-frills Fatih kebabçı — ~120-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Fatih is a conservative neighborhood — dress modestly. The Süleymaniye Mosque is free and stunning; arrive early morning for the best light and fewest visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — famous for its breathtaking Byzantine mosaics and frescoes (~200 TRY entry). Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood near the ancient Theodosian Walls. Walk a section of the historic land walls (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's colorful, photogenic Jewish and Greek Orthodox historic quarters. Wander the rainbow-painted staircase streets, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople (free), and browse antique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Golden Horn waterfront in Fener. Take a bus or tram back to the hotel. Enjoy a quiet evening meal in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Börek and tea at a Balat neighborhood bakery — ~50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Kumpir (loaded baked potato) from a street vendor in Balat — ~80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Manti (Turkish dumplings with yogurt and butter) at a local restaurant — ~120-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat is extremely photogenic and increasingly popular — visit on a weekday morning for a more authentic feel. Wear comfortable shoes for the hilly cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar). Take the public ferry from Kabataş (~50-80 TRY each way with Istanbulkart). Büyükada is the largest and most beautiful island. No motorized vehicles — rent a bicycle (~150-200 TRY for a few hours) or take a horse-drawn carriage to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada. Hike up to the Monastery of St. George for panoramic sea views (free, moderate hike). Relax on a small beach or swim in the Marmara Sea if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon ferry back to Istanbul. Enjoy the sunset views of the city skyline from the deck. Dinner near the ferry terminal.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and fruit from a local market before departure — ~40-60 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a simple waterfront lokanta on Büyükada — ~150-180 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek or a simple kebab near Kabataş ferry terminal — ~80-100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance for weekends as they fill up quickly. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket. The islands are a wonderful escape from the city bustle — very popular with locals on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace exterior and gardens (the palace interior is ~400 TRY but the waterfront promenade and clock tower are free). Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront, a lively local neighborhood with great street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş market area and the Çarşı neighborhood. Visit the Naval Museum (~100 TRY, excellent for history lovers with historic Ottoman galleys and maps). Walk up to Yıldız Park — a beautiful forested park with Ottoman pavilions (free entry to park).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the hip Ortaköy neighborhood along the Bosphorus. Admire the iconic Ortaköy Mosque with the Bosphorus Bridge as a backdrop. Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (stuffed baked potato) from street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Menemen and tea at a Beşiktaş neighborhood café — ~90-110 TRY
meals.lunch: Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from a street vendor in Beşiktaş — ~60-80 TRY for 10 pieces
meals.dinner: Kumpir at Ortaköy street market — ~100-130 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Beşiktaş is a favorite among Istanbul locals — great for people-watching and authentic street food. Ortaköy gets very crowded on weekends; visit on a weekday evening for a calmer experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Kadıköy neighborhood on the Asian side (ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy, ~25-40 TRY). Kadıköy is Istanbul's bohemian hub with a fantastic market, street art, independent coffee shops, and a vibrant food scene. Visit the Kadıköy Bazaar (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Moda, the charming seaside suburb of Kadıköy. Stroll the waterfront promenade, relax in Moda Park, and enjoy views of the Princes' Islands. Browse the indie bookshops and vintage stores.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Kadıköy's excellent restaurant scene for dinner before taking the ferry back. The neighborhood is famous for its meyhanes and craft beer bars.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at a Kadıköy kahvaltı spot — ~100-130 TRY
meals.lunch: Kokoreç sandwich and fresh juice at the Kadıköy market — ~80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Meze and grilled fish at a Kadıköy meyhane — ~180-220 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is a must-visit for foodies — the market has incredible fresh produce, cheeses, olives, and street food. It's also one of Istanbul's most progressive and LGBTQ-friendly neighborhoods.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum in Karaköy (~200 TRY, excellent for contemporary Turkish art). Then walk along the Karaköy waterfront and explore the trendy Tophane neighborhood with its historic cannon foundry and hip cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu (~150 TRY) — famous for its collection of Orientalist paintings and the iconic 'Tortoise Trainer' painting. Explore the Pera neighborhood's historic apartment buildings and art nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening shopping and souvenir hunting in the Grand Bazaar area or Arasta Bazaar (near the Blue Mosque, less touristy and better prices). Enjoy a farewell dinner in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Croissant and Turkish coffee at a Karaköy specialty café — ~80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Tantuni (spicy meat wrap) from a street stall in Beyoğlu — ~70-90 TRY
meals.dinner: Full traditional Turkish dinner — kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) at a Sultanahmet restaurant — ~200-250 TRY as a special farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: The Arasta Bazaar behind the Blue Mosque is less crowded and more authentic than the Grand Bazaar for souvenir shopping. Turkish coffee and tea make excellent lightweight gifts to bring home.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last Turkish breakfast. Take a final walk along the Bosphorus waterfront near the hotel. Pack and check out. If time allows, visit a neighborhood you missed or revisit a favorite spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 2-3 hours before departure). Take the metro or Havaist bus from the city center to Istanbul Airport (budget option, ~80-100 TRY vs expensive taxi). Check in and clear security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Browse the airport's duty-free for any last-minute Turkish delight or baklava. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final simit and tea from a street cart or hotel — ~30-50 TRY
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or pack leftovers from a bakery — ~80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport is large — allow extra time for walking between terminals. Keep some Turkish Lira for any last transport or food costs. Consider downloading offline maps before leaving the hotel Wi-Fi. Budget summary tip: Istanbul is very affordable — daily costs of 400-600 TRY (excluding accommodation) are very achievable covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in and settle into your room.

meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the hotel upon arrival — most mid-range hotels offer a late-night menu. Alternatively, grab a simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from an airport kiosk before your transfer.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — focus on a smooth arrival. Pre-arrange airport transfer with your hotel in advance to avoid taxi confusion late at night. Exchange a small amount of currency or use an ATM at the airport for initial expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront promenade near the resort to get your bearings and breathe in the Bosphorus or Sea of Marmara air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby neighborhood to explore local streets. Visit a local bazaar or covered market to get a feel for Istanbul street life. Pick up fresh fruits, spices, or small souvenirs. If near the Asian side, explore Kadıköy Market — a vibrant, authentic neighborhood market beloved by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront at sunset. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) near the hotel area with meze plates and fresh fish.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — enjoy Turkish staples like olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, and çay (tea).
meals.lunch: Casual köfte sandwich or lahmacun (Turkish flatbread with minced meat) from a local eatery near the bazaar — budget-friendly and delicious.
meals.dinner: Meyhane near the waterfront — order a spread of cold and warm mezes (hummus, stuffed grape leaves, fried calamari) and a grilled fish main. Budget around 300–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag recovery is important. Use the afternoon to orient yourself to the neighborhood. Download the Istanbul public transport app (İstanbulkart) and consider getting an İstanbulkart transit card for the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural achievements, originally a Byzantine cathedral, later an Ottoman mosque, and now a functioning mosque open to visitors. Arrive early (opens at 09:00) to beat the crowds. Dress modestly and bring a head covering for women.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii), just a few minutes from Hagia Sophia. Admire its six minarets and stunning Iznik tile interior. Then explore the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople — the Egyptian Obelisk, Serpent Column, and German Fountain are all free to view.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Sultanahmet neighborhood on foot as the sun sets. Enjoy dinner in the historic district at a mid-range Ottoman cuisine restaurant.

meals.lunch: Simit Sarayı or a local börek shop near Sultanahmet — try spinach or cheese börek with ayran (yogurt drink). Quick, cheap, and authentic.
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant or a similar mid-range Ottoman restaurant in Sultanahmet — try lamb tandir, Ottoman pilaf, and baklava for dessert. Budget around 400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free to enter but requires modest dress. Blue Mosque is free. Sultanahmet is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes. Avoid touts outside these attractions offering 'free tours.'

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) — the magnificent imperial palace of the Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. Explore the Harem, Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the stunning views over the Bosphorus from the palace terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down the hill to Gülhane Park — Istanbul's oldest public park, originally the outer garden of Topkapi Palace. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) nearby, housing incredible ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) area for evening shopping and atmosphere — though the bazaar itself closes around 19:00, the surrounding streets remain lively. Dinner in the Beyazıt or Eminönü neighborhood.

meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — a historic institution serving traditional Turkish food with Bosphorus views. Mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant near Eminönü — famous for its kebabs and rooftop views of the Golden Horn. Try the Adana kebab or lamb shish. Budget around 400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace entrance fee applies (approximately 500–700 TL); Harem is an additional ticket. The palace complex is large — wear comfortable shoes and allow 3–4 hours. The Archaeological Museums are a hidden gem often missed by tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, jewelry, spices, and textiles. Practice your bargaining skills! Opens at 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) in Eminönü for an aromatic experience of Turkish spices, dried fruits, nuts, Turkish delight, and teas. Explore the bustling Eminönü waterfront and watch the ferries cross the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot — watch fishermen casting lines from the bridge — and walk up to the Galata Tower neighborhood (Karaköy). Explore the trendy streets of Karaköy and Galata for the evening.

meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the famous floating boats at Eminönü waterfront — an iconic Istanbul street food experience. Pair with a cup of turşu suyu (pickle juice). Very affordable.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası or a similar modern Turkish bistro in Karaköy — known for elevated takes on traditional dishes. Budget around 400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is free to enter. Bargaining is expected — start at about 50–60% of the asking price. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas. The Galata Bridge walk is free and offers fantastic views.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the European side's Beyoğlu district and visit the Galata Tower — a medieval stone tower offering panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul. Then explore the charming, hilly streets of the Galata neighborhood with its antique shops and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard stretching 1.4 km through the heart of Beyoğlu. Ride the historic Tünel funicular (one of the world's oldest underground railways). Explore the side streets (Çiçek Pasajı, Balık Pazarı fish market passage) and discover bookshops, music stores, and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Continue exploring Beyoğlu's vibrant nightlife area around Nevizade Street — lined with meyhanes spilling out onto the street. A lively, social evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local Istanbul bakery (fırın) for a fresh simit with cheese and tea — the quintessential Istanbul breakfast on the go.
meals.lunch: Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) area — try the historic Haci Abdullah Restaurant or a local meyhane for a proper sit-down lunch with meze and grilled meats.
meals.dinner: Nevizade Sokak meyhane street — pick any of the lively taverns, order a selection of mezes, fresh fish, and enjoy the buzzing atmosphere. Budget around 350–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Galata Tower has an entrance fee (approximately 300–400 TL). İstiklal Avenue is always crowded but safe. The historic red tram runs along İstiklal Avenue — a fun photo opportunity. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Beyoğlu is very hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus Ferry Cruise — one of Istanbul's most iconic experiences. Board a public ferry (şehir hatları) from Eminönü or Beşiktaş for the full Bosphorus tour to Anadolu Kavağı, passing under the Bosphorus bridges, alongside waterfront yalıs (wooden mansions), and Rumeli Fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian shore — a charming fishing village at the mouth of the Bosphorus. Hike up to the medieval Yoros Castle (Genoese Castle) for sweeping views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to the European side. Arrive back in the city as the sun sets over the skyline. Relaxed dinner near the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the ferry departure.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the waterfront fish restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı — the village is famous for its fish. Try levrek (sea bass) or çupra (sea bream) with salad and bread. Budget around 300–500 TL per person.
meals.dinner: Casual waterfront restaurant near Eminönü or Beşiktaş — try midye dolma (stuffed mussels) as a street snack, followed by a simple dinner of grilled meat or fish.

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is very affordable (approximately 50–80 TL each way with İstanbulkart) and far more authentic than expensive private tours. The full round trip takes most of the day. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water. Yoros Castle is free to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus, featuring 285 rooms, 44 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. Guided tours are mandatory and fascinating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel) to admire its exterior on the Bosphorus waterfront. Then explore the upscale Beşiktaş neighborhood — a vibrant local district with a famous open-air market. Visit the Beşiktaş fish market and surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Ortaköy neighborhood — famous for its picturesque mosque on the Bosphorus waterfront and its street food scene. The area is especially beautiful at night with the illuminated Bosphorus Bridge in the background.

meals.lunch: Local lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) in Beşiktaş — point-and-choose from ready-made dishes like lentil soup, stuffed peppers, braised lamb, and rice. Authentic and very affordable (150–250 TL per person).
meals.dinner: Ortaköy waterfront restaurants — enjoy dinner with views of the illuminated Bosphorus Bridge. Try a mid-range fish or meyhane restaurant. Also try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) as a street snack.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires purchasing a ticket (approximately 600–800 TL) and joining a guided tour — book online in advance if possible. Photography is restricted inside. Ortaköy is best visited in the evening when it comes alive with street vendors and visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul and explore Üsküdar — one of Istanbul's most traditional and authentic neighborhoods. Visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, stroll along the waterfront, and see the iconic Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) from the shore (or take a short boat to visit it).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry or bus to Kadıköy — Istanbul's hippest and most vibrant neighborhood on the Asian side. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Moda area), browse independent bookshops, vinyl record stores, and artisan coffee shops. Visit the covered food market for an incredible array of local produce, cheeses, and deli items.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Kadıköy nightlife scene — the neighborhood has excellent bars, live music venues, and restaurants. A great place to mingle with young Istanbul locals.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a kahvaltı salonu (breakfast salon) in Üsküdar or Kadıköy — a full spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), tomatoes, and fresh bread. Budget around 200–350 TL per person.
meals.lunch: Kadıköy Market food stalls — graze on fresh produce, sample local cheeses, try kokoreç (seasoned offal in bread) if adventurous, or have a quick lahmacun.
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant famous for preserving forgotten Anatolian recipes. An absolute must for food lovers. Budget around 300–500 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Asian side of Istanbul feels noticeably different from the European side — more residential, less touristy, and very authentic. Çiya Sofrası is highly recommended and often cited as one of Istanbul's best restaurants — arrive early as it gets busy. The Maiden's Tower boat trip is a short, inexpensive excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque (Süleymaniye Camii) — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque, designed by the great Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan and built for Suleiman the Magnificent. The hilltop location offers stunning views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) with its medrese, hamam, and tombs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fatih and Zeyrek neighborhoods — among Istanbul's oldest and most historically layered districts. Visit the Zeyrek Mosque (formerly the Byzantine Church of the Pantocrator), and wander the wooden Ottoman-era streets. These neighborhoods are largely off the tourist trail.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Pierre Loti Hill (Pierre Loti Tepesi) in Eyüp by cable car for panoramic views over the Golden Horn, especially beautiful at sunset. The hilltop café has been serving tea since the 19th century.

meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe Restaurant near Süleymaniye Mosque — a historic Ottoman imaret (soup kitchen) converted into a restaurant serving traditional Ottoman dishes in a beautiful courtyard setting. Mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: Local meyhane or kebab restaurant in the Fatih district — try İskender kebab (döner on bread with tomato sauce and yogurt) or a simple pide (Turkish flatbread pizza). Budget around 250–400 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Süleymaniye Mosque is free to enter but requires modest dress. The Fatih and Zeyrek neighborhoods are best explored on foot — the streets are steep and cobbled, so wear good shoes. Pierre Loti cable car has a small fee. Eyüp is also home to one of Istanbul's most sacred mosques — dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) in Sultanahmet — a stunning underground Byzantine cistern built in the 6th century, featuring 336 marble columns and atmospheric lighting. Then visit the nearby Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi), which houses spectacular Byzantine floor mosaics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arasta Bazaar — a quieter, more authentic alternative to the Grand Bazaar, located behind the Blue Mosque. Browse quality Turkish ceramics, carpets, and textiles without the aggressive tourist-market pressure. Then visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Turkish bath (hamam) — a quintessential Istanbul cultural experience. The historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or Çağaloğlu Hamamı are excellent mid-range options near Sultanahmet.

meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — a legendary restaurant near the Hippodrome serving only one thing: köfte (meatballs) with white beans and bread. Simple, historic, and delicious. Very affordable.
meals.dinner: After the hamam, enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet with views of the illuminated Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque — a magical Istanbul evening. Budget around 400–600 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: Basilica Cistern has recently been renovated and is more impressive than ever — book tickets online to skip the queue (approximately 400–500 TL). Hamam prices range from 600–1,200 TL for the full treatment including scrub and massage — the experience is absolutely worth it. Book the hamam in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii / Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, dating from the 14th century. A true hidden gem compared to the main tourist sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls (Land Walls of Constantinople) — the massive 5th-century Byzantine fortifications that protected Constantinople for over a thousand years. Explore the Edirnekapı and Yedikule sections. Visit Yedikule Fortress (Yedikule Hisarı) — the Ottoman fortification built into the ancient walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center for a final evening of exploration. Visit the vibrant Karaköy and Tophane neighborhoods for contemporary art galleries (Istanbul Modern Museum is nearby) and trendy bars and restaurants.

meals.lunch: Local neighborhood restaurant near Edirnekapı — try a simple home-style Turkish lunch at a family-run lokanta. Dishes like mercimek çorbası (lentil soup), kuru fasulye (white bean stew), and pilaf. Very affordable (150–200 TL per person).
meals.dinner: Karaköy or Tophane area — try Zuma Istanbul (splurge option) or a more casual mid-range contemporary Turkish restaurant. Alternatively, explore the street food scene in Karaköy — kokoreç, midye dolma, and dürüm wraps.

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access depending on its current status as a mosque — check in advance. The Theodosian Walls are free to walk alongside. Yedikule Fortress has a small entrance fee. This is a great day for history enthusiasts who want to go beyond the standard tourist circuit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot you didn't have enough time for. Alternatively, visit the Princes' Islands (Adalar) for a half-day escape: take a ferry from Kabataş to Büyükada (the largest island), where no cars are allowed and horse-drawn carriages and bicycles rule the streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the islands (or from your morning activity) and do any last-minute shopping. The Arasta Bazaar or the boutique shops in Galata/Karaköy are ideal for quality Turkish ceramics, hand-painted tiles, Turkish delight, specialty teas, and artisan goods. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant to celebrate your Istanbul journey. Choose a memorable rooftop or Bosphorus-view restaurant for a final memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: One last traditional Turkish breakfast — if you haven't tried a full kahvaltı spread yet, Van Kahvaltı Evi in Cihangir is famous for its lavish breakfast platters.
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the Princes' Islands — fresh fish or a simple salad at a waterfront café on Büyükada. Or a quick street food lunch if staying in the city.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mikla Restaurant (rooftop, panoramic Istanbul views, modern Turkish-Nordic cuisine) or Asitane Restaurant (Ottoman palace cuisine) — both are special occasion mid-to-upper-range restaurants. Budget around 600–1,000 TL per person for a memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Princes' Islands ferry from Kabataş takes approximately 1–1.5 hours (İstanbulkart accepted). Büyükada is beautiful in May with blooming flowers and mild weather — rent a bicycle to explore the island. If skipping the islands, use the morning for the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy, which has an excellent collection of Turkish contemporary art. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange airport transfer in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort, Istanbul (Beachfront). Check-in, champagne welcome, and settle into your suite.

meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — charcuterie board, Turkish mezze platter, and a glass of local Kavaklidere wine to unwind after travel

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm VIP check-in with the resort concierge. Keep the first night relaxed — no early morning commitments the next day to allow recovery from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort followed by a private orientation tour of the Beachfront and surrounding Bosphorus waterfront. Take in panoramic views of the strait and get acquainted with the neighborhood. Optional: a short private boat ride along the Bosphorus to see Istanbul's skyline from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the Bosphorus shore. Arrange a private guided tour to explore the grand ceremonial halls, crystal staircase, and the room where Atatürk passed away. Stroll through the manicured palace gardens afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Tuğra Restaurant inside the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — one of Istanbul's most prestigious dining venues set in a restored Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus. Enjoy classic Ottoman-Turkish cuisine with impeccable service and water views.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — simit, beyaz peynir, olives, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), fresh pastries, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Casual waterfront lunch at a premium Beşiktaş fish restaurant — grilled sea bass, calamari, and fresh meze with Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Tuğra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace Kempinski — Ottoman lamb dishes, stuffed vine leaves, and traditional desserts like kazandibi

day_by_day.notes: Book the Dolmabahçe Palace private guided tour in advance. Reserve Tuğra Restaurant well ahead — it is extremely popular. Dress code at Tuğra is smart elegant.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Topkapi Palace — the nerve center of the Ottoman Empire for over 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics pavilion with a knowledgeable private historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the adjacent Gulhane Park, then explore the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex — three world-class museums housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and Islamic art collections. Finish with a stroll along the historic peninsula waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of a boutique hotel in Sultanahmet with panoramic views of the Bosphorus and Marmara Sea. Dinner at Matbah Restaurant — a refined Ottoman palace cuisine restaurant near the Grand Bazaar, serving recipes from the original Topkapi Palace kitchens.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Topkapi Palace's Konyali Restaurant — a historic institution within the palace grounds serving traditional Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant — Ottoman tasting menu featuring dishes like hünkarbeğendi (sultan's delight), lamb with dried fruits, and palace-style desserts

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Topkapi Palace tickets with Harem access in advance — queues can be very long. A private guide is strongly recommended to bring the history to life. Comfortable walking shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Hagia Sophia — the architectural marvel that has served as a Byzantine cathedral, Ottoman mosque, museum, and active mosque. Arrange an early-morning private access tour before crowds arrive to fully appreciate the breathtaking mosaics, dome, and layered history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — admire the stunning Iznik tile interior and six minarets. Then visit the Basilica Cistern — the atmospheric 6th-century underground Byzantine water reservoir with dramatic lighting and ancient Medusa column bases.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus dinner cruise on a luxury yacht — sail past illuminated palaces, mosques, and bridges as the sun sets over the city. Enjoy a curated Turkish and Mediterranean dinner on board with wine pairing.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Sultanahmet) — elegant Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine in a beautifully converted Ottoman prison building
meals.dinner: Private luxury Bosphorus yacht dinner — fresh seafood, mezes, Turkish wines, and desserts served on deck

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia requires modest dress (head coverings for women). Early morning private access must be arranged through a premium tour operator. Book the private yacht dinner cruise at least a week in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. A private guide will navigate you through the best artisan workshops, antique dealers, and authentic carpet and kilim galleries away from the tourist traps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar) — explore stalls overflowing with Turkish spices, lokum (Turkish delight), dried fruits, and teas. Then take a private Turkish cooking class at a premium culinary studio in the Old City — learn to prepare classic dishes like imam bayıldı, börek, and baklava.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Neolokal — one of Istanbul's most celebrated modern Anatolian restaurants located in the historic SALT Galata building. Chef Maksut Aşkar reinterprets traditional Anatolian flavors with contemporary technique.

meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a historic lokanta (traditional Turkish eatery) near the Grand Bazaar — slow-cooked stews, lentil soup, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Neolokal — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring innovative Anatolian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Agree on prices before purchasing in the Grand Bazaar even with a guide. The cooking class should be booked in advance — choose a class with a maximum of 6 participants for a premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private boat to Büyükada, the largest island. Explore by horse-drawn carriage (fayton) or bicycle through pine-scented streets lined with grand Victorian-era wooden mansions. Visit the historic Aya Yorgi Monastery on the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the island — enjoy the car-free tranquility, browse local artisan shops, and take in Marmara Sea views. Return to Istanbul by private boat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ulus 29 — a legendary Istanbul restaurant perched on a hilltop in the Ulus neighborhood with sweeping Bosphorus views. Known for its refined Turkish cuisine, celebrity clientele, and spectacular sunset dining.

meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — fresh grilled fish, octopus salad, and cold mezes overlooking the Marmara Sea
meals.dinner: Ulus 29 — signature dishes include sea bass carpaccio, lamb chops, and milk pudding desserts with panoramic Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Private boat to the Princes' Islands is far more comfortable than the public ferry. Book Ulus 29 well in advance — it is one of Istanbul's most sought-after reservations, especially for sunset tables.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury hammam (Turkish bath) experience at the historic Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — the most magnificent Ottoman bathhouse in Istanbul, built by Sinan in 1556. Book a private suite for an exclusive kese (exfoliation) and köpük (foam massage) treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beyoğlu district — walk the famous İstiklal Avenue, visit the historic Galata Tower for panoramic city views, and explore the charming backstreets of Galata and Karaköy with their independent galleries, concept stores, and artisan coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a deeply spiritual Sufi ritual performance. Then dinner at Mikla Restaurant — rooftop fine dining atop the Marmara Pera Hotel with 360-degree city views and Chef Mehmet Gürs's acclaimed New Anatolian cuisine.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Karaköy Lokantası — a beloved neighborhood restaurant in Karaköy serving elevated Turkish home cooking in a stylish setting
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant — tasting menu with wine pairing; signature dishes include lamb tartare, Aegean herbs, and wild sea bass

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ayasofya Hamamı private suite well in advance — it is the most prestigious hammam experience in Istanbul. The private Sema ceremony can be arranged through a luxury tour operator for a more intimate experience than public shows.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque — the magnificent 16th-century imperial mosque designed by the legendary Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan. Explore the complex including the tombs of Sultan Süleyman and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Walk through the historic surrounding neighborhood of Süleymaniye.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, recently restored and reopened. Then explore the ancient Theodosian Walls — the massive 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for a thousand years.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Pierre Loti Café — a legendary hilltop café in Eyüp with sweeping views over the Golden Horn, accessible by historic cable car. Dinner at Asitane Restaurant — adjacent to the Chora Church, specializing in meticulously researched Ottoman palace cuisine based on 15th and 16th-century recipes.

meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) near the Süleymaniye — enjoy rakı, cold mezes, and grilled fish in an authentic setting
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant — Ottoman tasting menu featuring dishes like stuffed melon, saffron lamb, and historic dessert recipes

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have limited access hours — confirm before visiting. Pierre Loti Café is best visited around sunset for the views. Asitane is one of Istanbul's most unique culinary experiences — reserve in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Pera Museum — a world-class art museum in Beyoğlu housing the famous Osman Hamdi Bey painting 'The Tortoise Trainer,' Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. A curated private tour brings the collections to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's most fashionable district with luxury boutiques, designer stores, and elegant cafés. Visit the Istanbul Modern (relocated to its stunning new Renzo Piano-designed waterfront building) for contemporary Turkish art.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at a rooftop bar in Beyoğlu. Dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar — a long-standing Istanbul institution in Ulus with spectacular Bosphorus views, serving premium steaks, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine list.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Nişantaşı — dine at a premium neighborhood restaurant such as Meze by Lemon Tree, known for creative Turkish mezes and seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Sunset Grill & Bar — prime rib, fresh Aegean fish, and Turkish wines with panoramic Bosphorus sunset views

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern has a premium café with harbor views — worth a stop. Nişantaşı is excellent for luxury shopping if interested. Sunset Grill requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day Bosphorus villages excursion — hire a private guide and vehicle to explore the charming historic villages along the European and Asian shores. Begin with Ortaköy — famous for its ornate baroque mosque, artisan market, and kumpir (stuffed baked potato) stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Bosphorus to Arnavutköy and Bebek — elegant waterfront neighborhoods with beautiful wooden yalı mansions, boutique shops, and waterfront cafés. Cross to the Asian side via private boat to explore Anadolu Kavağı and the medieval Yoros Castle ruins with sweeping Black Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side. Dinner at Feriye Lokantası — a stunning waterfront restaurant in a historic 19th-century palace pavilion in Ortaköy, serving refined Ottoman and Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views.

meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a premium fish restaurant in Bebek — fresh Bosphorus catch, grilled sea bream, and cold mezes with water views
meals.dinner: Feriye Lokantası — Ottoman-inspired dishes, fresh fish, and traditional desserts in a historic waterfront setting

day_by_day.notes: A private vehicle is essential for this day to move efficiently between Bosphorus villages. The Asian shore crossing by private boat adds a memorable experience. Yoros Castle involves some uphill walking — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Topkapi Palace Imperial Treasury and Pavilion of the Holy Mantle (if not fully explored on Day 3). Alternatively, visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts — a beautifully curated museum in a 16th-century Ottoman palace on the Hippodrome, housing exceptional carpets, calligraphy, and ethnographic collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Hippodrome of Constantinople — the ancient chariot racing arena and social heart of Byzantine Constantinople. See the Egyptian Obelisk, Serpent Column, and German Fountain. Then visit the Mosaic Museum — displaying magnificent Byzantine floor mosaics from the Great Palace of Constantinople.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner experience — arrange a bespoke private dining setup on a terrace overlooking the illuminated Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia at night. Many luxury hotels offer this exclusive arrangement for premium guests.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Balıkçı Sabahattin — one of Istanbul's most beloved traditional fish restaurants near the Sultanahmet area, serving impeccably fresh seafood since 1927
meals.dinner: Private bespoke rooftop dinner with personal chef and butler service — customized Turkish and Mediterranean menu with curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The private rooftop dinner must be arranged through the resort concierge or a luxury experience operator at least 3-4 days in advance. This is one of the most magical dining experiences Istanbul can offer.

day_by_day.morning: Private Turkish food market tour — visit the Fatih Market or a local neighborhood bazaar with a private food guide. Learn about seasonal Turkish produce, spices, cheeses, and street foods. Sample everything from fresh simit to gözleme (stuffed flatbread) and freshly pressed pomegranate juice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private masterclass in Ottoman calligraphy or Ebru (Turkish paper marbling) art — a deeply traditional Turkish art form, led by a master artisan in a historic atelier. Take home your own handcrafted piece as a unique souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, watching the Bosphorus at twilight. Final dinner at Carne — a premium steakhouse and Mediterranean restaurant, or alternatively at Vogue Restaurant in Beşiktaş — a sleek rooftop venue with stunning views and a sophisticated menu of Turkish and international cuisine.

meals.lunch: Lunch at a hidden gem meyhane discovered during the morning market tour — enjoy fresh dishes prepared with market ingredients in an authentic local setting
meals.dinner: Vogue Restaurant — premium tasting menu featuring Aegean-inspired dishes, fresh seafood, and an exceptional wine and cocktail list with Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: The calligraphy or Ebru masterclass should be booked in advance through a cultural tour specialist. The food market tour is best done in the morning when markets are most vibrant. Vogue Restaurant requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort — enjoy a long breakfast, take a last walk along the Bosphorus beachfront, and soak in the views. Optional: a final coffee at a waterfront café in the neighborhood and last-minute souvenir shopping for premium Turkish items — handmade ceramics, quality Turkish delight, saffron, or a hand-knotted silk carpet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Aegean Bliss Resort with private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport. Allow ample time for Istanbul traffic, especially during afternoon hours. Enjoy the VIP airport lounge before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Carry with you 13 days of extraordinary Ottoman history, Bosphorus sunsets, world-class cuisine, and the timeless magic of a city where East meets West.

meals.breakfast: Final grand Turkish breakfast at the resort — a full spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, pastries, honey, kaymak, and Turkish tea to end the trip on a high note
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a quick bite at a nearby café before transfer — lahmacun, ayran, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board meal — the resort concierge can arrange a premium departure meal package

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically noon — arrange a late check-out if the flight schedule allows. Istanbul traffic can be unpredictable; allow at least 3 hours before flight departure for the airport transfer. Ensure all purchases (carpets, antiques) have proper documentation for customs.
